title: Closed bounded-degree loci for a separated etale chart
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with atlas topology on field-valued point classes [def-a1-space-point-topology] and sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A geometric point is a map $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ from an algebraically closed field [def-weil-geometric-point], and its geometric fibre is the sheaf fibre product with this map. Quasi-compact means quasi-compact on scheme tests, or, for a space, that every open cover has a finite subcover. Quasi-separated means that the absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. Separated for a morphism means that its diagonal is representable by closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Etale means representable etale on scheme tests [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Integral means representable and integral on scheme tests [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; in particular its pullback to an affine scheme is affine. Open immersions are representable by open immersions on scheme tests [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $f:W\to X$ be a quasi-compact separated etale morphism with $W$ a scheme. Suppose some integer $N$ bounds the cardinalities of all geometric fibres. For every integer $r\geq0$, the subset $D_r\subseteq|X|$ of points with geometric fibre cardinality at most $r$ is closed. Consequently, if a dense open subspace $O\subseteq X$ has all these cardinalities at most $r$, the same bound holds on all of $X$.

source.place: Tag 07S8 (lemma-quasi-compact-reasonable-stratification), etale specialization of its closed degree filtration.

proof.text: Fix $r\geq0$ and put $m=r+1$. Construct $P_1=W$ and $P_{k+1}=P_k\times_XW$ for $1\leq k<m$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] these are algebraic spaces and each $P_{k+1}$ is a scheme, since $P_k$ is a scheme and $W\to X$ is representable etale. The projection $P_{k+1}\to P_k$ is a base change of $f$. The base-change and composition clauses of [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] therefore prove inductively that $P_k\to X$ is etale. Its scheme source makes this representable etale. Write $p_1,\ldots,p_m:P_m\to W$ for its coordinates. On every test scheme its sections are exactly $m$ sections of $W$ with a common image in $X$, by the fibre-product universal property.

For each $1\leq i<j\leq m$, pull back $\Delta_f:W\to W\times_XW$ along $(p_i,p_j):P_m\to W\times_XW$. Separatedness in the hypothesis says precisely that this scheme test is a closed immersion $E_{ij}\to P_m$. Its image is closed by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $C_m$ be the open subscheme of $P_m$ complementary to the finite union of these images [def-pc-scheme]. A field-valued tuple factors through $E_{ij}$ exactly when its two coordinates agree: this is the diagonal pullback universal property. It factors through $C_m$ exactly when none of those equalities holds. Indeed a map from a field spectrum factors through an open subscheme precisely when its single image point lies in the open, by the restriction description of [def-weil-open-immersion]. For $m=1$ the union is empty and $C_1=W$.

source.place: Separation-axiom definition of a separated morphism; finite pairwise equality loci from its diagonal, expanded directly on scheme tests.

proof.text: The inclusion $C_m\hookrightarrow P_m$ is an open immersion of schemes, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1). Compose it with $P_m\to X$ using [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]; the resulting $q_m:C_m\to X$ is representable etale since its source is a scheme. Apply [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] to obtain its open image $I_m\subseteq X$. That node also says that for every $g:G\to X$ the point image of $C_m\times_XG\to G$ is the pullback open $I_m\times_XG$.

source.place: Tag 03IR (lemma-etale-open), with the arbitrary-base-change image clause of Tag 03H4 (lemma-points-cartesian); morphisms.tex Tag 02GP (lemma-open-immersion-etale).

proof.text: Let $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ be any geometric point. Its pullback $W_{\bar x}$ is an etale scheme over $\Omega$, by representability of $f$. By the first clause of [lem-kun-0ezp], $W_{\bar x}$ is a disjoint union of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. This clause applies because an algebraically closed field is separably closed. Each point is thus one distinct $\Omega$-valued section. Evaluating the fibre products of step 1 at $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, and removing the equality loci of step 2, identifies the $\Omega$-sections of $(C_m)_{\bar x}$ with ordered $m$-tuples of pairwise distinct points of $W_{\bar x}$. Also $(C_m)_{\bar x}$ is etale by base change, so the same first clause says it is nonempty if and only if it has an $\Omega$-section. The image-base-change clause of [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] now gives $x\in|I_m|$ if and only if $(C_m)_{\bar x}$ is nonempty, equivalently $|W_{\bar x}|$ has at least $m$ points. In particular the inequality is independent of the chosen geometric representative. As $m=r+1$, this proves $|I_m|=|X|\setminus D_r$.

source.place: Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field), clause (1); etale-cohomology.tex Tag 09Z9 (lemma-normal-scheme-with-alg-closed-function-field), field specialization underlying the first clause of lem-kun-0ezp.

proof.text: Step 3 makes $|I_{r+1}|$ open, so step 4 makes $D_r$ closed. If $O$ is the dense open in the statement, its point set is contained in $D_r$. Every closed subset containing a dense subset contains its closure, namely all of $|X|$. Thus $D_r=|X|$, proving the final assertion. The argument includes $r=0$ (the complement is the image of $W$), the empty base, the empty chart, and $r\geq N$ (then no tuple of $r+1$ distinct fibre points exists).

source.place: Tag 09YB (lemma-there-is-a-scheme-integral-over), strict degree-decrease paragraph following the invocation of Tag 07S8; the closure inference is elementary.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NR-43ced3ab0 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full; it has 5 steps and no new nodes, the statement is unchanged, and proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. The proof forms the (r+1)-fold chart product P_m and removes the pairwise diagonal pullbacks E_ij. These are closed by the item's own separatedness hypothesis, which leaves an open C_m. The étale image I_m is open, and its base-change clause (lem-a1-space-etale-open-image) identifies the geometric fibre of C_m with ordered (r+1)-tuples of distinct fibre points. That fibre description uses the first clause of lem-kun-0ezp, which is valid because objects of the small étale site are all étale U→T and an algebraically closed field is separably closed. So |I_{r+1}| = |X| minus D_r, and the dense-open clause follows. Two small implicit steps are standard and need no repair: a field point lying in the image of a closed immersion factors through it, and the base change of an open immersion is an open immersion. Source check: Stacks decent-spaces Tag 07S8 (line 1436) and the proof of Tag 09YB (lines 1855-1866, where the degree of a quasi-compact étale map does not rise under specialization, applied with a dense open). The item matches this exactly; there is no SGA citation. Small cases: W = X⊔X gives D_1 empty; an open immersion gives D_0 = X minus U; empty X or W, r=0 and r≥N all work. The affine line with doubled origin shows separatedness is needed, and step 2 uses it. No duplicate: the a1 affine diagonal-complement and groupoid rank-strata nodes are scheme or finite-locally-free statements.
